hero.name: Sanghyeon Shin
hero.lead: A service planner who doesn't stop at the spec.
hero.summary: I **design with policies and specs**, **build the tools** that are missing, and check the results in front of real users. Most recently, as an intern at LIKELION, I co-designed the judging policy and feature specs for a **2,000-person hackathon** and built **three ops tools** that went live on site.

about.description_1: I'm a service planner who stays with the work until it holds up in front of real users, not just on paper.
about.description_2: I started in **frontend development**. At LIKELION, the part I loved most was **zero to one**: an idea turning into a screen, then shipping and watching people use it. When I joined the 13th cohort's staff, my questions changed from 'how do we build this' to **'who uses it, why, and how does it become a business'**, and that led me into service planning.
about.what_sub: Service planning at the core, with as much design, building, and operating as the work needs.
about.description_3: The **14th national hackathon**, which I worked on as an intern at LIKELION, shows this best. I co-designed the **judging policy and platform feature specs** with the team, and to make the 'no edits after deadline' rule actually hold, I **built a tool that scanned 562 repos and caught 5 violating teams**.
about.closing: I want to keep asking what experience people will have with a service, and what one thing will set it apart.
about.training: SSAFY 15th cohort, Non-CS Java track, completed (Jan – Apr 2026)

items.t: Build agreement with policy and specs
items.d: I designed a three-stage judging funnel and a 100-point rubric, mapping submission items 1:1 to criteria so teams could predict how they'd be judged. Two feature specs went to the dev and design teams in an As-Is → To-Be format. All of this was co-designed with the team.

items.t: Build the tools that are missing
items.d: 562 repos couldn't be checked by hand. I built the submission checker, the finals console, and the FAQ bot, and put them to work on site.

items.t: Test hypotheses in front of users
items.d: The first hypothesis, 'paying is inconvenient', broke in interviews with working accountants. We moved to the real problem, manual vouchers after payment, and placed 5th of 102 teams.
